name: steps
summary: A wizard/stepper — a numbered progress track through the ordered stages of a multi-step flow, showing which steps are done, which is current, and which remain.
selectHint: Use for a linear multi-step flow (a create/import wizard, a guided form). NOT for switching between peer sections of one page (that is obs-tabs), and NOT for navigating between pages (obs-breadcrumbs / obs-sidebar).
whenToUse: A task split into an explicit, ordered sequence of stages the user advances through — a wizard, a guided setup, a staged import — where showing progress and completed/remaining steps matters.
insteadOf: a hand-built row of numbered circles + connector divs
tabs used to fake a sequential flow (tabs are non-linear peers)

variants.name: horizontal
variants.what: Numbered circle + label with a connector line, laid left-to-right (default). The Report wizard form.

variants.name: vertical
variants.what: A left-rail stepper: steps stack top-to-bottom with title + optional description. The compliance rules form.

variants.name: number
variants.what: The marker shows the step index (or a ✓ when finished / ✗ on error). Default marker style.

variants.name: dot
variants.what: A compact state-dot track (Ant progressDot) — no number, just a coloured dot per state.

variants.name: outline
variants.what: Lined circles: a transparent circle with a coloured ring + number/✓ (fill="outline"). A lighter treatment for dense pages.

variants.name: circles-only
variants.what: Just the progress circles — no labels, no connector lines (compact + connector="none"). A compact indicator; completed can be primary/black or green.

sizes.name: default
sizes.note: Ant default marker; comfortable horizontal wizard.

sizes.name: small
sizes.note: Matches the compliance form rail; denser vertical wizards.

states.name: wait
states.what: A future step — muted marker + label; not yet reachable.

states.name: process
states.what: The current step — --primary fill with an OUTER GREY RING (halo) so it stands out.

states.name: finish
states.what: A completed step — --primary fill + ✓ marker. NOT green; the label + the connector after it stay grey.

states.name: error
states.what: A failed step — --secondary-red marker + label (per-item status or the current step's `status`).

items.note: the steps: [{label, description?, status?}] or a plain ["A","B"] / comma-list. status overrides the derived state (e.g. 'error').

active.note: the current step index (0-based). Steps before it derive to finish, after it to wait.

direction.note: horizontal — a left-to-right wizard bar; vertical — a stacked left-rail stepper (with descriptions).

variant.note: number — index/✓ circle; dot — a compact coloured state dot.

size.note: default 32px marker; small 24px (the compliance form rail).

clickable.note: when true, completed/current steps are navigable (pointer + hover); clicking emits `change` with the index. Future steps stay inert.

status.note: the status of the CURRENT (active) step — set 'error' to flag that the current stage failed validation.

fill.note: solid — a filled circle marker (default); outline — a lined circle (transparent fill, the colour on the border + number/✓) for a lighter look.

connector.note: line — connecting lines between steps (default); none — hide the lines (e.g. a circles-only progress track).

completed.note: colour of COMPLETED (finish) markers: primary (black/navy, default) or green (--secondary-green). The current step stays primary.

compact.note: hide the labels/descriptions → a compact circles-only progress track (pair with connector="none" to drop the lines too).

events.name: change
events.note: emitted when a clickable step is selected; payload is the step index (Vue custom-element wraps it — read detail[0]).

decisionFlow: Switching between independent peer sections of the SAME page (Overview / Metrics / Logs)? -> obs-tabs, NOT steps (steps imply an ordered sequence).
Navigating between different pages / a location trail? -> obs-breadcrumbs or obs-sidebar, NOT steps.
An ordered multi-step flow the user advances through (wizard, guided setup, staged import)? -> obs-steps.
Is it a compact horizontal bar at the top of a form? -> direction="horizontal" (the default; the Report wizard).
A side rail with per-step descriptions and back-navigation? -> direction="vertical" + clickable (the compliance form).
Dense/secondary flow where numbers add noise? -> variant="dot".
State: set `active` to the current index; mark a failed stage with a per-item status:"error" (or the `status` prop for the current step).
Want a lighter, outlined circle instead of a solid fill? -> fill="outline".
Want just the progress circles (no labels, no lines) — a compact indicator? -> compact + connector="none" (set completed="green" or "primary").
Should completed steps read GREEN instead of primary/black? -> completed="green".

horizontal.useWhen: a wizard with a handful of stages that reads well as a top-of-form progress bar
horizontal.dontUse: steps have long descriptions or there are many of them (use vertical), or the flow isn't ordered (use tabs)
horizontal.example: the Report builder: Report Properties -> Visualizations & Preview -> Schedule

vertical.useWhen: a form wizard with a side rail, where each step benefits from a description and the user can jump back
vertical.dontUse: horizontal space is plentiful and steps are short (a horizontal bar is lighter)
vertical.example: the compliance Rule form: General -> Rules -> Notification -> Review, in a left MCol rail

dot.useWhen: a compact/secondary progress indicator where step numbers would be visual noise
dot.dontUse: the user needs to read step labels/numbers to know where they are (use number)
dot.example: a dense inline progress track (Ant progressDot style)

clickable.useWhen: the flow allows revisiting completed steps (edit an earlier answer) without losing state
clickable.dontUse: steps must be completed strictly in order and cannot be revisited
clickable.example: the compliance form lets you click a completed step to go back; future steps stay disabled

outline.useWhen: a lighter stepper on a dense page / when a solid filled circle is too heavy
outline.dontUse: the default filled circle reads fine (solid has more presence)
outline.example: fill="outline" — a transparent circle with a coloured ring + number/✓

circles-only.useWhen: a compact progress indicator where labels + lines add noise (e.g. a tight header, a card corner)
circles-only.dontUse: the user needs step names to understand the flow (keep labels)
circles-only.example: compact connector="none" completed="green" — five circles, done ones green, no text/lines

number.useWhen: a wizard where users benefit from seeing the step index / a ✓ on completion (the default)
number.dontUse: a dense/secondary track where numbers are noise (use dot) or a bare progress indicator (circles-only)

error.useWhen: a stage FAILED and the user must fix it before continuing (validation error, failed import)
error.dontUse: the step is merely incomplete/pending (that is the wait state, not error)
error.example: items=[{label,status:"error"}] for a specific step, or status="error" for the current step

size.useWhen: small (24px) for a dense side rail (the compliance form) or a tight space; default (32px) for a top-of-form wizard bar
size.dontUse: small on a spacious horizontal wizard (the markers look cramped)

completed.useWhen: green when a done/success reading is wanted (a positive completion signal); primary/black for a neutral progress look
completed.dontUse: green if the flow is not really success-framed (primary is the safe default)
completed.example: completed="green" — done steps read green, the current step stays primary

connector.useWhen: line (default) to show the sequence as a connected track; none to drop the lines for a circles-only / segmented look
connector.dontUse: none when the sequential relationship between steps must be visually obvious
connector.example: connector="none" — used with compact for a circles-only indicator

compact.useWhen: space is tight and step names are not essential (a header, a card corner, a toolbar) — show circles only
compact.dontUse: the user needs the step labels to understand where they are
compact.example: compact connector="none" — five circles, no text, no lines

usage.note: Approximate — the product renders steppers as bespoke forms (report-steps.vue, rules-form.vue) plus the .counter-steps Ant-Steps style; obs-steps consolidates them into one contract. Counts are file-level, not instance-level.

do: Use steps only for an ordered, sequential flow — a wizard, not peer sections.
Keep `active` in sync with the current stage; let finished/remaining states derive from it.
Give each step a short, action-oriented label (Report Properties, Schedule) — add a description in the vertical form.
Mark a failed stage with status:"error" so the user sees where it broke.
Enable clickable only when revisiting a completed step is actually safe.
dont: Don't use steps to switch between independent sections of one page (that's obs-tabs).
Don't use steps for page-to-page navigation (obs-breadcrumbs / obs-sidebar).
Don't let a user jump to a future/unreached step (keep them inert).
Don't hardcode the state colours — the green/primary/red derive from tokens.

a11y.summary: An ordered progress list: the track is role="list", each step role="listitem", and the current step carries aria-current="step". State is conveyed by more than colour (a ✓ for done, the index for pending, ✗ for error), so it survives colour-blindness and greyscale.
a11y.notes: Keyboard/pointer: when clickable, completed + current steps are actionable (click emits `change` with the index) and future steps are inert (cursor: not-allowed) — a consumer should make the actionable steps focusable + Enter/Space activatable and never let a user jump to an unreached step. Announce progress: keep aria-current on the active step and, in a live wizard, consider an aria-live "Step N of M" announcement on change. Do not rely on colour alone — the marker glyph (✓ / number / ✗) and the disabled affordance back up the primary/green/red. Contrast: the ✓/number uses --primary-button-text (the on-primary colour) so it stays legible on the marker fill in BOTH light and dark themes. In the dot / circles-only forms (no glyph), pair the dots with an adjacent text label or an aria-label so the current step is discernible without colour.

knownIssues: Fixed (2026-07-20): in DARK theme the completed ✓ (and the current-step number) were invisible — the marker fill resolves to a LIGHT colour in dark theme while the glyph was hardcoded #fff. Now the glyph uses --primary-button-text (the theme-aware on-primary colour), so it stays readable on the light circle in both themes.

Source-derived reproduction: obs-steps consolidates the product's three bespoke steppers (report-steps.vue horizontal wizard, rules-form.vue vertical rail, the .counter-steps Ant style) into one MSteps-aligned contract. There is no single isolated Storybook story to pixel-diff against, so the element was built to the transcribed source values (report-steps 50px circle / dashed --neutral-light connector / green+primary fills; rules-form 24px circle + ✓; steps.less status connector colours) and verified behaviourally + eyeballed. Marker default size is 32px (Ant default) rather than the report form's 50px, which reads oversized for a general stepper.
